# Blend Mic

> Blend Mic is a free, open source (MIT) virtual microphone for Mac. It mixes your voice with a call or any app's sound into one microphone, so a local dictation app such as Handy or OpenSuperWhisper can transcribe both sides of an online call, even with headphones on. Apple silicon, macOS 15 or later.

- Each mix is a microphone, named "Blend Mic (mix name)" in other apps, with a slider per source.
- Sources: any input device, one app, or all system audio. System audio leaves out the app using the mix, so a call never hears itself.
- Split mode puts the microphone on the left channel and the rest on the right, for apps that transcribe each side separately.
- Ducking, off by default, lowers the other sources by 12 dB while you speak.
- Up to 16 mixes.
- Added delay: about 30 ms, or about 75 ms with echo cancellation on, measured on Apple silicon.
- Installs a Core Audio plug-in that runs in user space, not a kernel extension. Uninstall in its settings removes it.
- Alternatives it replaces: BlackHole (free, no mixer, set up in Audio MIDI Setup) and Loopback ($99).
- Privacy: your audio stays on the Mac, no accounts, no analytics in the app.
